Bathroom Remodeling in Augusta, KS

Augusta's housing history spans more than a century and its bathrooms tell that story. The older homes near downtown — built during the oil boom years of the 1910s through 1940s — have original cast-iron plumbing, hexagonal mosaic tile floors, pedestal sinks, and claw-foot tub rough-in that was installed when Augusta was a prosperous oil town. These bathrooms have character. They also have 80-year-old cast-iron drain lines that are corroding from the inside, galvanized supply lines that have calcified to reduced flow, and subfloors that have absorbed water from slow leaks for decades.

The mid-century and later homes in Augusta have different problems — 1960s and 1970s bathrooms with original fiberglass surrounds that have long since passed their useful life, linoleum flooring that's lifting at seams, and vanities from the 1980s that a coat of paint can only hide for so long.

Wheatland Construction serves Augusta and Butler County. We're a Veterans Approved Builder (ID: 00899), Home Advisor Certified since 2019, and Butler County based since 2018. We've worked in Augusta's older housing stock and we know what century-old plumbing looks like when you open the walls.

Older Augusta Home Bathroom Remodeling

The pre-1950 homes near downtown Augusta are some of the most interesting bathrooms we work in — and some of the most demanding. A few realities:

Cast-iron drain lines: Original cast-iron in pre-1950 Augusta homes has a finite lifespan. When it goes, it fails slowly — pinhole leaks that saturate the subfloor before anyone notices. We camera-inspect drain lines in older Augusta homes before closing new tile over them.

Galvanized supply lines: Original galvanized steel supply lines in Augusta homes from the 1910s–1940s have been calcifying for 70–100 years. Flow is reduced; pressure at fixtures is lower than it should be. Copper or PEX replacement is usually worth doing during a remodel rather than having it fail after the walls are closed.

Character preservation: We don't gut old Augusta bathrooms and install generic contractor tile. When the original hexagonal mosaic is worth saving, we preserve it. When it needs to go, we find period-appropriate replacements. These homes have character that deserves respect.

Mid-Century and Later Augusta Bathrooms

1960s–1980s Augusta bathrooms are standard older remodel candidates — fiberglass surrounds replaced with tile, vanities updated, fixtures upgraded. We approach these straightforwardly: demo, moisture assessment of the subfloor and walls, proper waterproofing membrane, quality tile and materials, permitted plumbing and electrical.

Permits in Augusta

City of Augusta Building Department for homes inside city limits. Butler County for unincorporated properties. We determine jurisdiction and handle all permits.

How We Approach Bathroom Remodeling in

Every bathroom remodel in starts with an in-person assessment. We walk the existing bathroom with you, look at what's behind the walls where it matters (around the tub/shower surround, under the vanity, at the subfloor where it meets the tub), and give you an honest read on what the project actually involves before any numbers get discussed.

We price in writing. Every line item - demo, plumbing, tile, vanity, fixtures, exhaust, permit - is documented before work starts. No surprises mid-project.

Our crew handles demo through final walkthrough. We don't hand off your project to a rotating cast of subcontractors who don't know each other's work. The people who pull the permits are the people who do the work and stand behind it.

Wheatland Construction has held Veterans Approved Builder status (ID: 00899) since we opened and has been Home Advisor Certified since 2019. We're licensed and insured in Kansas. If something isn't right at the final walkthrough, we fix it before we consider the project done.

In Augusta, Butler County's largest city has a genuinely broad housing stock - oil-era downtown grid homes from the 1910s-1940s, mid-century ranches from the 1950s-1970s, and newer suburban additions off Highway 400. Each vintage has different renovation requirements.

Frequently Asked Questions About Bathroom Remodeling in Augusta

How much does bathroom remodeling cost in Augusta, KS?

Augusta bathroom remodels range from $7,500 for a straightforward guest bath refresh to $30,000+ for a full primary bath renovation in an older downtown home with plumbing infrastructure updates. Older homes with cast-iron or galvanized pipe are quoted with that scope separated. Written, line-item estimates.

Can older Augusta homes with original plumbing be remodeled?

Yes — we work in them regularly. We camera-inspect drains, assess supply line condition, and give you options for what needs to be updated now versus what can wait. We don't close walls over plumbing problems.

Who handles permits for bathroom remodeling in Augusta?

City of Augusta Building Department for in-city homes. Butler County for unincorporated properties. We handle all permit applications and inspections.

Do you preserve original tile and fixtures in historic Augusta homes when possible?

Yes — when original elements are in good condition and worth saving (original hexagonal mosaic, original hardware in serviceable condition), we incorporate them into the remodel rather than defaulting to full replacement. We discuss this at the consultation.

How long does a bathroom remodel take in Augusta?

2–5 weeks depending on scope. Older homes with plumbing infrastructure work take longer. We give you a realistic timeline upfront.

Does bathroom remodeling add value in Augusta?

Yes. Butler County real estate has appreciated and Augusta's housing market is active. Updated bathrooms improve appraised value and marketability, particularly in the older home market where buyers are often weighing the cost of deferred maintenance.
